content.overview: Section 7 sets out the process and documents required for incorporation before the Registrar of Companies. On registration and issue of the certificate of incorporation, the company comes into existence as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal (where adopted).
content.glance: List the documents to be filed under s. 7; state the Registrar’s role; note the effect of the certificate of incorporation and the company’s status from the date of incorporation.
content.study: Section 7 is the procedural heart of incorporation. Persons forming a company must file with the Registrar the memorandum and articles, a declaration of compliance, an affidavit from first directors, address for correspondence, particulars of subscribers and first directors, and other prescribed documents. The Registrar may accept or reject the documents. On registration, the Registrar issues a certificate of incorporation, which is conclusive evidence that all requirements of the Act in respect of registration have been complied with and that the company is duly registered. From the date of incorporation in the certificate, the subscribers and subsequent members become a body corporate by the name in the memorandum, capable of exercising the functions of an incorporated company with perpetual succession and a common seal (where it has one), and with power to hold property and to sue and be sued. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in s. 7 and the connected formation provisions (ss. 3–5).

sections.heading: Documents for Incorporation
sections.body: Memorandum, articles, compliance declaration, director affidavits, address, subscriber and director particulars, and other prescribed documents.

sections.heading: Registrar’s Scrutiny
sections.body: The Registrar examines the documents and may accept or refuse registration.

sections.heading: Certificate of Incorporation
sections.body: On registration the Registrar issues a certificate of incorporation, which is conclusive evidence of compliance with registration requirements and of due registration.

sections.heading: Effect of Incorporation
sections.body: From the date in the certificate, the company is a body corporate with perpetual succession, capacity to hold property, and capacity to sue and be sued.

examples.title: Complete filing
examples.body: All prescribed documents under s. 7 are filed in order. The Registrar registers the company and issues the certificate of incorporation.

examples.title: Defective declaration
examples.body: The compliance declaration is false or incomplete. The Registrar may refuse registration; post-incorporation consequences may also follow if fraud is later established.

hypotheticals.question: Is the certificate of incorporation conclusive for all purposes?
hypotheticals.analysis: It is conclusive evidence that registration requirements were complied with and that the company is duly registered. It does not validate illegal objects or protect against all forms of challenge in every context.

hypotheticals.question: When does the company come into existence?
hypotheticals.analysis: From the date of incorporation mentioned in the certificate issued under s. 7.

distinctions.title: Formation (s. 3) vs incorporation (s. 7)
distinctions.left: Agreement to form and subscription of memorandum
distinctions.right: Filing, registration and certificate creating the body corporate

rows.left: Who forms and on what terms

misconceptions.trap: Signing the memorandum incorporates the company.
misconceptions.correction: Incorporation occurs only on registration and issue of the certificate under s. 7.

misconceptions.trap: The certificate cures all illegality in the objects.
misconceptions.correction: The certificate is conclusive of registration compliance; it does not legitimise unlawful objects.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: A properly incorporated company was challenged as indistinct from its controlling shareholder.
cases.issue: What is the legal effect of incorporation?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A registered company is a legal person separate from its members.
cases.relevance: Authority already in the file; classic statement of the effect of incorporation.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 7 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. List required documents. II. State the Registrar’s role. III. Explain the certificate and its conclusiveness. IV. State the effect from the date of incorporation. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Document checklist; registration status; certificate analysis; effect of incorporation; precise relief.
